title: Saturn's Rings Are Disappearing Right Now (NASA Did the Math)

scenes.text: Saturn's rings are disappearing. Right now.
Every half hour, enough water falls out of them to fill an Olympic swimming pool.
NASA calls it ring rain. Charged ice slides down the magnetic field into Saturn's clouds.
scenes.keywords: saturn rings close up ice particles

scenes.text: At that rate the rings are gone in under 100 million years. And they may be only 100 million years old.
So the first dinosaurs may have seen a Saturn with no rings at all.
We're alive in the middle of their short life. Look now. They're disappearing.

description:
Saturn's rings are disappearing. Right now.
NASA scientists measured a ring rain of charged ice falling into the planet along its magnetic field, enough water to fill an Olympic swimming pool every half hour. At that rate the rings vanish in under 100 million years, and they may be only about 100 million years old, so the first dinosaurs may have seen a ringless Saturn.
Would you rather have lived before the rings, or now? Comment below.
first_comment: Bonus: Saturn is over 4 billion years old, but its rings may be younger than 100 million years. Would you rather have seen the solar system before the rings, or now?
